questions.q: In a certain code language, A + B means 'A is the sister of B', A @ B means 'A is the brother of B', A - B means 'A is the wife of B', and A # B means 'A is the father of B'. How is O related to V if 'O + P # T @ G - V'?
questions.solution:
O is the sister of P, and P is the father of T; T @ G makes T and G siblings, so P is G's father too and O is their aunt.
G - V makes G the wife of V, so O is the sister of V's wife's father.
**Answer: Wife's father's sister**
questions.shortcut: Decode pairwise: O = sister of P → P = father of T and G → G = wife of V; O is V's wife's paternal aunt.

questions.q: If + means -, - means ×, × means ÷ and ÷ means +, then what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the equation? 84 - 6 ÷ 371 + 648 × 8 = ?
questions.solution:
Substituting the symbols: $84 \times 6 + 371 - 648 \div 8$.
$84 \times 6 = 504$ and $648 \div 8 = 81$, so the value $= 504 + 371 - 81 = 794$.
**Answer: 794**
questions.shortcut: Swap symbols first, then BODMAS: 504 + 371 − 81.

questions.q: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 61, 85, 109, 133, 157, ?
questions.solution:
Every term increases by a constant 24: 61, 85, 109, 133, 157.
The next term is $157 + 24 = 181$.
**Answer: 181**
questions.shortcut: Constant difference +24 → 157 + 24.

questions.q: Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster DOES NOT belong to that group?
questions.solution:
In GKE, NRL and LPJ the letter steps are +4 then -6 (G+4=K, K-6=E; N+4=R, R-6=L; L+4=P, P-6=J).
In OSN the steps are +4 then -5, so it does not belong.
**Answer: OSN**
questions.shortcut: Test the gaps: three clusters follow +4, −6; OSN breaks the pattern.

questions.q: Alex starts from Point A and drives 8 km towards the east. He then takes a left turn, drives 6 km, turns left and drives 17 km. He then takes a left turn and drives 13 km. He takes a final left turn, drives 9 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again?
questions.solution:
East-west movement: $8 - 17 + 9 = 0$ km, so P lies due north-south of A.
North-south movement: $6 - 13 = -7$ km, so P is 7 km south of A; he must drive 7 km to the north.
**Answer: 7 km to the north**
questions.shortcut: Net east-west cancels to 0; net north-south = 6 − 13 = −7 → 7 km north.

questions.q: UI 12 is related to YK -2 in a certain way. In the same way, OL 9 is related to SN -5. To which of the following is PQ 15 related, following the same logic?
questions.solution:
Each letter shifts ahead: U+4=Y, I+2=K and O+4=S, L+2=N; the number falls by 14 (12 to -2, 9 to -5).
Applying the same to PQ 15: P+4=T, Q+2=S and $15 - 14 = 1$, giving TS 1.
**Answer: TS 1**
questions.shortcut: Letters +4, +2; number −14 → TS 1.

questions.q: In a certain code language, 'house sip head' is coded as 'bm ma px' and 'head wood robot' is coded as 'pz bm ey'. How is 'head' coded in the given language?
questions.solution:
'head' is the only word common to both statements and 'bm' is the only code common to both.
So 'head' is coded as 'bm'.
**Answer: bm**
questions.shortcut: Common word → common code: head–bm.

questions.q: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (14, 42, 3) (12, 60, 5)
questions.solution:
In both given sets, first × third = middle: $14 \times 3 = 42$ and $12 \times 5 = 60$.
Only $13 \times 3 = 39$ follows the same relation.
**Answer: (13, 39, 3)**
questions.shortcut: Check first × third = second: 13 × 3 = 39.

questions.q: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series, based on the English alphabetical order? RJV QIU PHT OGS ?
questions.solution:
Each letter moves one step back from term to term: R-Q-P-O-N, J-I-H-G-F, V-U-T-S-R.
So the next cluster is NFR.
**Answer: NFR**
questions.shortcut: −1 to each letter per term: after OGS comes NFR.

questions.q: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Statements: Some hats are caps. No cap is a vest. Conclusions: (I) Some hats are vests. (II) Some caps are hats.
questions.solution:
'Some caps are hats' is the valid converse of 'Some hats are caps', so (II) follows.
(I) does not follow: the hats that are caps can never be vests, and nothing guarantees any other hat is a vest.
**Answer: Only conclusion (II) follows.**
questions.shortcut: A 'some' statement converts fully; the hat-cap overlap is cut off from vests.

questions.q: Seven people, A, B, C, D, E, F and G, are sitting in a row, facing north. Only five people sit to the right of A. Only five people sit to the left of B. F is an immediate neighbour of G and E. C sits second to the left of E. How many people sit to the right of G?
questions.solution:
Five people to the right of A put A 2nd, and five to the left of B put B 6th, leaving seats 3-5 for the G-F-E trio with F in the middle.
C sits second to the left of E, which forces E 3rd, F 4th, G 5th, C 1st and D 7th: the row is C, A, E, F, G, B, D.
Only B and D sit to the right of G.
**Answer: Two**
questions.shortcut: Fix A=2, B=6; the trio must be 3-4-5 and C = E − 2 pins E=3, F=4, G=5.

questions.q: Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster DOES NOT belong to that group?
questions.solution:
In UTR, IHF and NMK the steps are -1 then -2 (U-T-R, I-H-F, N-M-K).
In ZZW the steps are 0 then -3, so it does not belong.
**Answer: ZZW**
questions.shortcut: Letter gaps −1, −2 in three clusters; ZZW fails.

questions.q: Madhur ranked 58th from the top and 6th from the bottom in his class. How many students are there in his class?
questions.solution:
Total students $= 58 + 6 - 1 = 63$, since Madhur is counted in both ranks.
**Answer: 63**
questions.shortcut: Top rank + bottom rank − 1.

questions.q: If 'A' stands for '÷', 'B' stands for '×', 'C' stands for '+' and 'D' stands for '-', what will come in place of the question mark '?' in the following equation? 15 A 3 B 10 C 8 D 12 = ?
questions.solution:
Substituting: $15 \div 3 \times 10 + 8 - 12$.
$15 \div 3 \times 10 = 50$, so the value $= 50 + 8 - 12 = 46$.
**Answer: 46**
questions.shortcut: ÷ and × first: 5 × 10 = 50, then +8 − 12.

questions.q: Seven people B, C, D, I, J, K and L are sitting in a straight line facing north. Only two people sit to the right of C. Only two people sit between C and B. Only two people sit between D and K. Only three people sit between C and D. J sits to the immediate right of I. How many people sit to the left of L?
questions.solution:
Two people to the right of C put C 5th; B then sits 2nd (two between), D 1st (three between D and C) and K 4th (two between D and K).
J is immediately right of I, so I and J take seats 6 and 7, leaving L the 3rd seat: the row is D, B, L, C, K, I, J.
Only D and B sit to the left of L.
**Answer: Two**
questions.shortcut: Fix C=5, B=2, D=1, K=4; I-J fill 6-7 and L lands 3rd.

questions.q: Ajay starts from Point A and drives 16 km towards the west. He then takes a right turn, drives 8 km, then turns left and drives 7 km. He then takes a left turn and drives 8 km. He takes a final right turn, drives 2 km, and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again?
questions.solution:
Facing west, his right turn points north (8 km); then left means west 7 km, left means south 8 km, and the final right means west 2 km.
North and south cancel ($8 - 8 = 0$) and the westward legs add to $16 + 7 + 2 = 25$ km.
So P is 25 km west of A and he must drive 25 km towards east.
**Answer: 25 km towards east**
questions.shortcut: Vertical legs cancel; add all west legs: 16 + 7 + 2 = 25.

questions.q: Radhika ranked 21st from the top and 7th from the bottom in her class. How many students are there in the class?
questions.solution:
Total students $= 21 + 7 - 1 = 27$.
**Answer: 27**

questions.q: Which of the following letter-number clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete? HBE22 ICF29 JDG36 KEH43 ?
questions.solution:
Letters advance by 1 each term (H-I-J-K-L, B-C-D-E-F, E-F-G-H-I) and the numbers rise by 7: 22, 29, 36, 43, 50.
So the missing cluster is LFI50.
**Answer: LFI50**
questions.shortcut: +1 to each letter and +7 to the number → LFI50.

questions.q: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 616 610 612 606 608 ?
questions.solution:
The series alternates $-6, +2$: $616 \to 610 \to 612 \to 606 \to 608$.
The next term is $608 - 6 = 602$.
**Answer: 602**
questions.shortcut: −6, +2 alternating → 608 − 6 = 602.

questions.q: RR 4 is related to UQ -14 in a certain way. In the same way, II 8 is related to LH -10. To which of the given options is MO 12 related, following the same logic?
questions.solution:
The first letter moves 3 ahead and the second 1 back (R+3=U, R-1=Q; I+3=L, I-1=H), and the number falls by 18 (4 to -14, 8 to -10).
Applying this to MO 12: M+3=P, O-1=N and $12 - 18 = -6$, giving PN -6.
**Answer: PN -6**
questions.shortcut: Letters +3, −1; number −18 → PN −6.

questions.q: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Statements: Some pizzas are cupcakes. All buns are cupcakes. Conclusions: (I) Some pizzas are buns. (II) All cupcakes are buns.
questions.solution:
The pizzas and the buns can be two separate groups inside the cupcakes, so (I) does not follow.
'All buns are cupcakes' cannot be reversed, so (II) does not follow either.
**Answer: Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows.**
questions.shortcut: 'All' never converts; two sets inside a bigger one need not overlap.
